decisions.reason: The firm has sunk tooling and catalogue investment into this multi-model lever family, and two years is too early to judge uptake given long architectural specification cycles.
The mitred family visibly expresses the firm's proprietary engineering and design identity, so management will attribute modest results to the slow project pipeline rather than withdraw it.
The multifunctional handle sits at the heart of the announced barrier-free system direction, which makes dropping it hard to justify publicly.

It is embedded in the coordinated handle ranges and planning documentation that planners rely on, so keeping it protects earlier commitments despite some range-pruning pressure after Product E's removal.
The finish costs little to maintain, applies across families and showcases in-house finishing expertise, so there is little reason to withdraw it.
